title: Iterative Refinement
definition: The process of continuously improving a solution through repeated cycles of analysis, correction, and re-evaluation.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a sculptor who chisels away at a block of stone, gradually shaping it into a beautiful statue. The sculptor keeps examining their work, making corrections, and repeating the process until they're satisfied. This is similar to iterative refinement in computer science.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In the context of machine learning, iterative refinement involves training a model, evaluating its performance, identifying areas for improvement, and then retraining the model with the new insights. This cycle continues until the model's performance meets the desired standards.
difficulty_levels.expert: Iterative refinement is a fundamental concept in computer science, with applications ranging from artificial intelligence to software engineering. It's also closely related to the scientific method, as it involves a cycle of hypothesis testing, experimentation, and revision. The novel insight is that iterative refinement can be applied to complex systems, such as a knowledge graph, to improve its accuracy and completeness over time.

extra_fields.insight: The continuous improvement and refinement of the knowledge graph through iterative processes, such as data cleaning, deduplication, and mapping.
